payload.selection_rationale: The practice proposal is selected as its core, with four amendments. It matches what the survey measured: the four SL-043 entries exist in .taad/fitness.yaml (lines 191-219) and in their xUnit twins, rules-parity is AGREE, and plants.json has 35 rows with none for these rules. Spike sl043-four-twinned-rules-each-caught-by-plant already ran four plants through the real harness with the real engine, and all four came out AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits and a quiet baseline. So the slice is data only: four JSON rows, the `_note` counts, any literal counts in RuleCases.ps1, and one fresh recording run. Adding a harness `--record` mode, changing the row schema, or giving the scratch copy a code graph would be over-built and would break the `_note` rule that outcomes are changed by hand only, from recorded runs. The practice designer raised no over-engineering flag. Amendments: (1) the spike record shown to design is clipped after X01 and partway through X02, so the transcription of X03 and X04 is a shortcut. The evidence is the fresh `--scenario all` run against the edited tree. A row may be re-derived if the record cannot be recovered, provided it is labelled re-derived and the run passes. (2) If the recording run cannot be made, the rows are not committed. Guessed outcomes are what this slice exists to eliminate. (3) The RuleCases.ps1 edit is a search-then-run: grep for 35, 19, 48, 52 and the F-row IDs, bump what counts plants.json rows, and run the script, because the survey did not list the literals. (4) The four IDs are F20-F23, and the spike's X01-X04 names are not used.

components.name: Four new plant rows (F20-F23)
components.responsibility: F20 is TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags (*.cs), with a named link-tag constant such as `private const uint IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK = 0xA000000C;` planted in src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/EntryClassifier.cs. F21 is NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core), with a blocking wait on the volume figure such as `_store.VolumeUsedSource.Task.Wait();` planted in Core. F22 is NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App), with a blocking wait planted in the App file the spike used. F23 is TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore (*.cs), with a ScanStore reference planted in src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/VolumeSpace.cs. Each row expects both twins to fire (the Fitness entry and the xUnit Fact) and carries exactly the keys F17-F19 carry. F20, F21 and F23 list their settled SL-043 twins in `also_settled`. F23 also lists 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'. Plant text and anchors come from the full spikes#62 record, or from the kept scratch plants-spike.json if it survives. If a row cannot be recovered, it is re-derived from the fitness.yaml patterns and the xUnit twins and labelled re-derived. The design was not shown the plant text or anchors for F22 and F23, so they are not invented here.
components.key_interactions: harness.py copies the working tree to a scratch tree, applies each plant, builds with dotnet, reads the trx and runs taad3.fitness, then judge() requires that every named rule fires and nothing else does. An unlisted extra hit is STRAY-HIT. EntryClassifier.cs already carries plants P07d and D3 for OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute, so F20 must not disturb those rows.

components.name: plants.json `_note` counts
components.responsibility: Change the prose counts from 35 rows and 19 must-fire to 39 rows and 23 must-fire. The rule that outcomes are changed by hand only, from recorded runs, stays word for word.
components.key_interactions: Prose only, and harness.py does not read it. The counts reconcile as 35+4=39 and 19+4=23 (F01-F19 become F01-F23). With divergences.json's 13 rows the `--scenario all` total moves from 48 to 52.

components.name: RuleCases.ps1 count literals
components.responsibility: Find every literal that counts plants.json rows or must-fire rows, or lists their IDs, and move it by +4. A count that is already derived from the file is left alone. Literals are not converted to baseline-derived values here. SL-069 owns that for the parity sites.
components.key_interactions: C-006 to C-014 need the engine and exercise recorded rows. Run the script after the edit. A stale literal fails a case rather than passing silently.

components.name: Recording run
components.responsibility: One run against the edited tree, kept as the slice's evidence: `%APPDATA%\taad3\venv\Scripts\python.exe eng/rules-harness/harness.py --engine-root C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend --root <SL-075 tree> --dotnet-from <worktree with a populated .dotnet/, e.g. ...\filesystem-analyser-v2-wt\SL-074> --scenario all`. Pass means exit 0, the stdout header shows taad3.fitness loaded from <engine-root>\taad3\fitness.py, all 52 rows AS-RECORDED (0 MISSED, 0 STRAY-HIT), and a quiet clean baseline (11 Facts pass, 64 rules, 0 hits). Save stdout, the exit code, the engine HEAD and the dotnet source.
components.key_interactions: harness.py is not edited. It requires --engine-root (harness.py:10 and :702) and raises CannotMeasure if the fitness module is not loaded from the engine root. The Fitness verdict is 'unable', not 'pass', because the import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' is NOT RUN without a code graph. That is the harness's normal not_run_on_scratch case and is accepted.

components.name: Guarded rules (read-only)
components.responsibility: The four fitness entries and their xUnit twins that the plants must trip. This slice does not edit them.
components.key_interactions: Entries at lines 191-219. The Facts are in ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, where one Fact covers both the Core and App halves of NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure. rules-parity.ps1 must still print AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns.

components.name: Run evidence record
components.responsibility: Holds the recording run's stdout, exit code, engine HEAD (faecfc3 or the current one) and dotnet source. It is written after the run finishes. Nothing is added under eng/.
components.key_interactions: The harness copies untracked, non-ignored files into its scratch tree, so evidence containing a .cs file written before the run could be seen by a *.cs rule.

contracts.name: plants.json row schema
contracts.notes: Used unchanged. It is a contract with two consumers, harness.py and RuleCases.ps1. The new rows add no keys. They carry exactly the keys F17-F19 carry, plus `also`/`also_settled` wherever the plant also trips a twin. The spike confirmed all four plants fit without editing harness.py.
contracts.error_cases: A rule string that does not match the engine's rule name gives MISSED on the row plus STRAY-HIT on the unmatched hit. This matters most for the two entries that share the name NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure. A missing anchor makes the row unmeasurable. A plant that breaks the build for an unrelated reason leaves no rule-level verdict. Each of these fails the recording run, and none is fixed by editing the expected outcome.

contracts.name: harness.py recording invocation
contracts.notes: `<engine venv python> eng/rules-harness/harness.py --engine-root <taad_v3\backend> [--root <tree>] [--dotnet-from <tree with .dotnet/>] --scenario all`. This PC has only SDK 8.0.425 and 9.0.318, so a .NET 10 SDK comes from --dotnet-from a sibling worktree, or from the eng/dotnet.ps1 download authorised by Q-003.
contracts.error_cases: CannotMeasure if taad3.fitness does not come from the engine root. Non-zero exit if any row is not AS-RECORDED. Without an SDK, without --dotnet-from and without network the run cannot happen. In that case the rows are not committed, and an obligation goes back to the stage that owns the run.

contracts.name: RuleCases.ps1
contracts.notes: `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1` must exit 0 after the literal update, with the engine available for C-006 to C-014.
contracts.error_cases: A stale row-count literal shows up as a failing case.

contracts.name: rules-parity.ps1 (unchanged)
contracts.notes: `pwsh -NoProfile -File eng/rules-parity.ps1` must still print AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns, exit 0. This slice touches neither the yaml nor the Facts.
contracts.error_cases: DRIFT or CANNOT-READ means the tree changed under the slice. Stop.

key_decisions.decision: Four rows, one per fitness entry. NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure gets separate Core (F21) and App (F22) rows although one xUnit Fact covers both.
key_decisions.rationale: The Core and App entries have different globs, and one plant proves one of them. A single row would leave one entry unmeasured as a guard, which is the gap the slice exists to close. The build check counted four entries and the spike measured four rows. The xUnit fire on F21 or F22 cannot say which half caught the plant. The per-entry Fitness hits separate them.

key_decisions.decision: IDs are F20-F23, continuing the must-fire F-series. The spike's scratch names X01-X04 are not used.
key_decisions.rationale: The `_note` counts must-fire rows as the F-series (19 = F01-F19), and SL-040 extended it the same way with F17-F19. A new prefix would make the must-fire count ambiguous. Copy every key F17-F19 use, so whatever marks a row must-fire comes along.

key_decisions.decision: The evidence is a fresh `--scenario all` run against the edited working tree, with all 52 rows AS-RECORDED. Transcribing the spike's plant text is only a shortcut to get the rows written. If the run disagrees with the spike, stop and investigate, and never edit an outcome to match.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike ran a scratch plants-spike.json, and harness-engine-root-reproduces-recorded-plants covered only the existing rows, so the committed rows have not yet been measured as committed. The `_note` allows outcomes to change by hand only, from recorded runs. Running all scenarios also proves the 48 existing rows did not move.

key_decisions.decision: If the recording run cannot be made (no .NET 10 SDK reachable, no network, engine root missing), do not commit rows with guessed outcomes. Raise an obligation naming the build stage.
key_decisions.rationale: Criterion 2 of the slice is that outcomes come from a recorded run. Committing unmeasured rows under an F-series ID would look like measurement and be none, which is worse than the current honest 'unmeasured' state.

key_decisions.decision: The .NET 10 SDK comes from --dotnet-from a sibling worktree whose gitignored .dotnet/ already holds 10.0.401 (SL-074). If none is available, fall back to the eng/dotnet.ps1 download.
key_decisions.rationale: Both spikes measured that this PC has no machine-wide SDK 10. Q-003 authorised the download into a gitignored .dotnet/. Either route builds the harness's scratch copy, not the working tree.

key_decisions.decision: harness.py, the row schema and the fitness/xUnit rules are not changed, and there is no auto-record or `--update` mode.
key_decisions.rationale: The schema has two consumers (harness.py and RuleCases.ps1). The spike showed all four plants fit it as it is. An auto-writing mode would contradict the `_note`'s hand-only rule and invite blind re-approval of snapshots. Changing the schema later means migrating both consumers.

key_decisions.decision: RuleCases.ps1 literals are bumped by +4 where they count plants.json rows. They are not converted to baseline-derived values in this slice.
key_decisions.rationale: SL-069 owns the derive-from-baseline change for the parity sites (-ExpectFacts). The survey did not list which plant-count literals exist, so the edit is grep then run, and the run is the check that none was missed.

key_decisions.decision: Run evidence is written under .taad/slices/SL-075/ after the run finishes, with the engine HEAD recorded. Nothing new is committed under eng/. Engine HEAD is not written into plants.json.
key_decisions.rationale: There is no packaged taad3 to pin to, so outcomes hold for the taad_v3 checkout used. The harness copies untracked non-ignored files, so evidence written before the run could be read by a *.cs rule. A clean clone of the edited tree, as spike 1 used, is the alternative.

key_decisions.decision: A Fitness verdict of 'unable' on the scratch copy is accepted as a pass condition. The one rule not run is the import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks'.
key_decisions.rationale: Both spikes measured this as the harness's normal not_run_on_scratch case. It concerns a rule unrelated to SL-043. Giving the harness a code graph is a separate slice.

proposals.note: The only proposal fielded. The crossdomain and expert designers were not run for this slice. Taken whole, with four amendments: the clipped spike record makes transcription a shortcut only, a stop rule when the run cannot be made, RuleCases.ps1 literals found by search then run, and empty architecture_rules with the reason stated.

payload.coherence_check: One proposal, so there is no composition to check, and nothing here has yet survived a disagreement. The reviewer should argue with it first. The internal seams I checked are these. (1) Counts reconcile: 35+4=39 plants.json rows, 19+4=23 must-fire, 48+4=52 rows under `--scenario all` (the extra 13 are divergences.json rows, which are untouched). (2) The guarded yaml and Facts are read-only, so rules-parity must stay AGREE 11 <- 15, 27 patterns. Any other result means the tree moved under the slice. (3) `also_settled` is required on the rows for X01, X02 and X04 (F20, F21, F23), and F23 also needs 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'. The spike listed none for X03 (F22), which the proposal reproduces. (4) F20 plants into EntryClassifier.cs, which already holds P07d and D3 for OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute, and `also_settled` is what keeps that from being a STRAY-HIT. (5) The hand-only outcome rule and the recording run point the same way, with no auto-record path. (6) The run copies untracked files, and the evidence folder is written afterwards. Nothing was contested, and these were not contested by anyone: whether the F22 App-file anchor and the F23 plant text can be recovered from spikes#62 (the design was shown them clipped); whether RuleCases.ps1 has plant-count literals and where; whether the SL-074 worktree with .dotnet/ will exist at build time; and that the outcomes hold only for taad_v3 at the HEAD used, since there is no packaged engine to pin to. No architecture rule is set. The design settles no dependency direction and no forbidden text. It edits one JSON data file, one prose note and count literals in one script, and the only bans it adds (no auto-record mode, no guessed outcomes) are process rules that a path glob or regex cannot separate from correct code without me having read harness.py.

cases.behaviour: TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags fires on a hard-coded link tag
cases.shape: A named constant `private const uint IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK = 0xA000000C;` planted in EntryClassifier.cs, which also holds P07d and D3 plants for a different rule
cases.why: Both twins must fire, and the settled OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute twin must be listed in `also_settled`. Without that key the harness reports STRAY-HIT, and a plant in a file other rows use can disturb them.

cases.behaviour: NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) fires on a blocking wait
cases.shape: `_store.VolumeUsedSource.Task.Wait();` planted in a Core file. The App entry must stay silent.
cases.why: The Core entry has its own glob, and a Core plant that also trips the App entry, or the reverse, is a STRAY-HIT.

cases.behaviour: NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App) fires on a blocking wait
cases.shape: A blocking wait on the volume figure planted in the App project. The Core entry must stay silent, and the one xUnit Fact fails.
cases.why: Only an App-side plant proves the App entry works as a guard. The Fact covers both halves, so the per-entry Fitness hit is the only thing that says the App entry fired.

cases.shape: Two fitness entries share the name and differ by glob, and the row's rule string must tell them apart
cases.why: A near-miss string shows up as MISSED plus STRAY-HIT, but only at the recording run, so the run has to be read for both F21 and F22.

cases.behaviour: TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore fires on a ScanStore reference
cases.shape: A ScanStore reference planted in VolumeSpace.cs. The settled rule 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends' also fires.
cases.why: The row needs `also_settled` for both settled twins, or the harness reports STRAY-HIT. The spike found the ScanStore rule also fires on this plant.

cases.shape: The edited tree with no plant applied
cases.why: A guard that fires on the unplanted tree proves nothing about what it catches. The spike measured 11 Facts passing, 64 rules and 0 hits, and the committed tree must reproduce that.

cases.behaviour: Committed rows reproduce the spike's outcomes, and the old rows do not move
cases.shape: plants.json with 39 rows run under `--scenario all`, with divergences.json unchanged
cases.why: The spike ran a scratch plants file, and the other spike covered only the existing rows. Only a run of the committed file shows all 52 AS-RECORDED and that F01-F19 and the P and S rows did not shift.

cases.behaviour: The outcome comes from the TAAD engine at --engine-root
cases.shape: taad3.fitness importable from somewhere other than the engine root, such as the shared ~/.claude venv
cases.why: The slice's second criterion is a run through the engine. The stdout header must show taad3.fitness loaded from <engine-root>\taad3\fitness.py. Otherwise the harness raises CannotMeasure and the run is not evidence.

cases.behaviour: RuleCases.ps1 agrees with the new row counts
cases.shape: A literal 35 rows, 19 must-fire, or an ID list ending at F19, left unchanged after +4 rows
cases.why: A stale literal fails a case, and the survey did not list which literals exist. SL-069 showed literal counts in this script go stale on the first addition.

cases.shape: A tree where only plants.json and RuleCases.ps1 changed
cases.why: Anything other than AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns means the yaml or the Facts moved under the slice, and the rows are then measured against something else.

cases.behaviour: A row that omits a settled twin
cases.shape: A row for X01, X02 or X04 without its `also_settled` keys
cases.why: Not owed a separate test (material false). It is the harness's existing STRAY-HIT branch, harness.py is unchanged, and the positive recording run with the keys present is what discharges it.

cases.behaviour: Evidence written into the tree before the run
cases.shape: An untracked, non-ignored .cs file under .taad/slices/SL-075/ copied into the scratch tree
cases.why: Not owed a test (material false). The evidence is text and JSON written after the run, and spike 2 ran in place with the untracked folder present and was quiet.

cases.shape: --dotnet-from points at a missing tree and there is no network
cases.why: Not a test (material false). It is a branch of eng/dotnet.ps1, which is unchanged. The spikes measured both the borrowed-SDK route and the download route. If neither is available the response is the stop rule, not a test.

cross_domain_transfer.pattern: A plant is a hand-chosen mutant aimed at one guard. A guard counts as measured when its mutant is killed by exactly the rules named on the row, the unmutated baseline is killed by nothing, and the mutant still compiles so the kill comes from the rule and not the build.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: harness.py already implements this discipline in judge(): every named rule must fire, nothing else may, and the baseline must be quiet. This slice supplies four more mutants. The transfer is descriptive and adds no new machinery. It matters for the conditions a row must meet, each of which maps to an evidenced fact below.

invariants.precondition: Each plant compiles, and the targeted xUnit Fact is what fails, not the build
invariants.evidence: spikes#62: X01's trx shows 'EntryClassifier.cs:23 Failed' on the Fact, and the falsifier 'plant fails the build for an unrelated reason' was not hit on 4/4.

invariants.precondition: The unplanted baseline trips neither twin
invariants.evidence: spikes#62 baseline: xUnit 11 Facts, 11 passed, 0 hits. Fitness 64 rules, 117 files read, 0 hits.

invariants.precondition: Each mutant is killed only by the rules named on its row (no STRAY-HIT)
invariants.evidence: spikes#62: all four AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits, conditional on `also_settled` on X01, X02 and X04 and the extra ScanStore rule on X04.

invariants.precondition: The rows as committed in plants.json, not the spike's scratch plants-spike.json, reproduce those outcomes, and the existing 48 rows do not move
invariants.evidence: Checked only by the build's recording run with `--scenario all`. The spike ran a scratch file, and harness-engine-root-reproduces-recorded-plants covered only the existing rows.

invariants.precondition: A .NET 10 SDK is reachable for the scratch build
invariants.evidence: Conditional in both spikes: this PC has only SDK 8.0.425 and 9.0.318. Use --dotnet-from SL-074 or the eng/dotnet.ps1 download authorised by Q-003.

Llewellyn Falco (approval testing: expectations are approved from a real run, never guessed)

prior_art.pattern: Every control records whether it actually fires ('Does a control earn its place?'). A guard with no evidence of firing is treated as unproven, which is the state the four SL-043 rules are in until they have plant rows.
Rules are feedforward and sensors are feedback, and a rule can name a deterministic sensor as its companion. Here each fitness/xUnit twin is paired with a plant that proves the sensor fires.

Mutation testing (killed and survived mutants): a mutant killed by a compile error does not show the test works, and a mutant that trips unrelated tests is noise. That matches the harness's rules that a plant must fail the targeted Fact and not the build, and must produce no STRAY-HIT.

Approval/snapshot testing in CI mode: a missing expectation fails instead of being written automatically. Known failure mode: developers re-approve snapshots without reading them. This is why there is no auto-record mode and why a mismatch is investigated, not edited away.
